capture_kind: Final fresh packaged Win64 gameplay-camera capture

automated_capture_record.basis: checks.txt, counted independently; separate from the visual findings

review_method.description: All 22 chronological contact sheets inspected, plus 11 original 1600x900 JPEGs. Sheets use crop/downscale only; some tool previews were reduced further. No interpolation, generated imagery, video encoding or runtime was used for this review.
review_method.timing: audio_seconds and world_seconds are copied from frames.csv. phase_relative_seconds subtracts the first captured frame in that phase, not the exact event time.
review_method.public_artifacts: Only this manifest and the prose review are curated; raw JPEG grids and the full capture remain local.

findings.observed: Sparse, small dark-red floor stains remain fixed as the wounded infected walks away. A second stain becomes clearer during frames 00069-00075; the earlier stain persists. The attack effect near the player later in this window is not counted as another wound-trail deposit.
findings.limits: The selected interval shows a few deposits, not a continuous stream. It does not establish the full bleeding lifetime.

findings.observed: Compared with the early window, a wider red patch is exposed behind the shoulder/head in the late window and native frame 00504. The pool remains partly covered by the torso; separate smaller trail stains stay visible to its right.
findings.limits: The gap between the two dense windows was not reviewed. These images do not measure growth rate or prove continuity throughout the gap; a large fraction of the pool is occluded.

findings.observed: Visible infected advance toward the corner player with changing leg poses, then form a compact ring/queue. The late sequence shows local stepping and attacks while the player remains cornered.
findings.limits: Rear actors and feet overlap. Some queued actors continue stepping with little translation. The camera exposes a large black area outside the room.

findings.assessment: Visible use of side and rear aisles
findings.observed: The early sequence shows actors approaching around the left and right rack edges. Later, a queue occupies the wall-side passage and the aisle behind the racks. No gross through-rack jump is visible in these sampled frames.
findings.limits: Racks, other actors and the HUD occlude feet and several complete paths. The images cannot prove that every one of the 18 actors has an unobstructed route or never stalls. Dense queuing and overlapping silhouettes remain visible.

findings.assessment: Approach and bench-end crowd contact visible
findings.observed: Actors approach from the open floor and gather around the exposed end and sides of the bench. The late window retains visibly different positions around the bench, with a trailing queue and close-contact animation.
findings.limits: The close group obscures the player and individual foot contact. Long, low strides and repeated body silhouettes remain mechanical in appearance; this is not a final naturalism approval.

findings.observed: Both inspected windows show the player on a cleared floor with no visible corpse, severed part or blood reappearing. The early camera settles after the phase transition; native final frame 03068 shows zero remaining on the HUD.
findings.limits: The phase changes the player/camera position. The view alone cannot establish off-camera actor or component cleanup; that is a separate automated assertion.

exclusions: Phases 2-5 collapse, severed limbs, freeze/resume and pile settling are reviewed separately by the integration lead.
Phase 9 mixed-combat motion is outside this review.
Unselected frames and the intervals between dense windows were not inspected.
This is chronological saved-frame inspection, not real-time video playback, direct manual input, audio audition or a performance result.
No all-actor collision, exact foot-slip or long-duration navigation claim is inferred from the images.
